definitions.gloss: campaign promise, public pledge, manifesto commitment
definitions.explanation: A promise or commitment made publicly, especially by a politician or political party during an election campaign. Can also refer to any formal pledge made to the public.

examples.japanese: {選挙|せんきょ}{公約|こうやく}を{掲|かか}げる。
{公約|こうやく}を{守|まも}れなかった{政治家|せいじか}は{批判|ひはん}された。
examples.english: The politician who could not keep his campaign promises was criticized.

examples.japanese: {減税|げんぜい}を{公約|こうやく}に{掲|かか}げて{当選|とうせん}したが、{実現|じつげん}には{至|いた}らなかった。
examples.english: He was elected on a pledge to cut taxes, but it was never realized.

notes:
Primarily used in political contexts. Often discussed in terms of whether promises are kept or broken.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{公約|こうやく}を{掲|かか}げる (put forward a pledge)
・{公約|こうやく}を{守|まも}る (keep a promise)
・{公約|こうやく}を{破|やぶ}る (break a promise)
・{公約|こうやく}{違反|いはん} (violation of a pledge)
・{選挙|せんきょ}{公約|こうやく} (election promise)
・マニフェスト (manifesto — near-synonym borrowed from English)

In Japanese politics, {公約|こうやく} is the traditional term. The loanword マニフェスト gained popularity in the 2000s to emphasize more specific, measurable commitments.
